area: testbed hardening: cycle 159's launcher tests were Windows-only despite a cross-platform README promise

find.report_claim: the README promises both entry points -- 'double-click start-shooter.cmd (Windows) or run ./start-shooter.sh (macOS/Linux)'
find.live_evidence: tests/test_launchers.py ran `cmd /c` and `taskkill` unconditionally, so the suite would have failed on any macOS/Linux machine the README claims to support
find.consumer_evidence: a suite that only passes on one platform silently narrows the project's stated support; the first person to run it on Linux would see a failure unrelated to their change

read: every subprocess call in tests/ via AST
killed: deleting the .cmd tests on non-Windows: the batch file is still part of the product, so its static contract must be asserted everywhere
leaving the suite unguarded and documenting 'Windows only': that contradicts the README rather than fixing the mismatch
guarding with pytest.mark.skip on the whole module: five of the seven tests are platform-neutral and must keep running on POSIX
analyze.survivor: guard only the two tests that spawn cmd.exe, keep the five static assertions unconditional, and pin the guard by simulating POSIX in a subprocess

fix.shooter: tests/test_launchers.py adds `WINDOWS = sys.platform == "win32"` and a `needs_cmd` skipif applied to exactly the two tests that execute cmd.exe; the module docstring now states which half runs where; both bare Popen call sites document that their bound comes from communicate(timeout=) plus taskkill, since Popen takes no timeout argument

shooter.guard: a subprocess that forces sys.platform = 'linux' before importing the module reported WINDOWS False and exactly two guarded tests, both with skip_when_not_windows True -- so on POSIX the five static tests run and the two cmd.exe tests skip
shooter.subprocess_audit: an AST sweep over every tests/test_*.py found zero subprocess.run/call/check_output calls without timeout=, and two Popen calls whose bound comes from communicate(timeout=RUN_TIMEOUT) plus taskkill /F /T
